market_question: US x Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: A permanent peace deal ending military hostilities between the US and Iran by June 30, 2026, is unlikely given decades of deep-seated enmity and the limited scope of recent de-escalation. The April 2026 temporary ceasefire extension suggests willingness to avoid immediate conflict but falls far short of a lasting agreement. Even if negotiations ramp up, complex issues (sanctions, nuclear program, regional proxies) make a comprehensive permanent deal improbable in just two months, leaving true probability around 10%, well below the market's 26.5%.
evidence_points: No US-Iran permanent peace precedent; relations marked by hostility since 1979.
Recent April 2026 deal was only a two-week ceasefire extension, not a permanent peace agreement.
Key sticking points (sanctions, Iran's nuclear ambitions, support for proxies) remain unresolved with no reported breakthrough.
